events.description: With the release of sensor version 7.11, CrowdStrike introduced the new IPC Template Type, delivered as Rapid Response Content via Channel File 291; its definition expected 21 input fields while the sensor code supplied only 20.

Manual and automated testing, stress testing, and WHQL-related validation of the IPC Template Type were performed; the automated tests used a wildcard matching criterion in the 21st field, and no fault was triggered.

A Template Instance for the IPC Template Type was released to production as part of a Rapid Response Content update; the first several field deployments succeeded and used wildcard matching for the 21st input.
Two additional IPC Template Instances were deployed, one introducing a non-wildcard matching criterion for the 21st input, producing a new version of Channel File 291.
The Content Validator evaluated the new Template Instances based on the expectation of 21 inputs, and the new Channel File 291 was sent to sensors.

events.time: July 19, 2024 (at the next IPC notification after receipt)
events.description: Windows sensors receiving the new Channel File 291 evaluated the Template Instances, attempted to read the 21st input value, performed an out-of-bounds memory read, and the system crashed with a PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA bugcheck in csagent.sys.
Recovery status measured: using week-over-week comparison, approximately 99% of Windows sensors were online compared to before the content update (typical variance about 1%).
